key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive degradation screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface damage and improving UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different perovskite depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements under UV soaking.
Compare perovskite films and devices with different ITO interface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements locate preferential degradation at the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and indicate improved UV stability after interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or evidence that UV-soaking results generalize to long-term outdoor operation.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
